Q116273823.summary: Cut into a small faceted piece of rock crystal, Christ hangs on a cross with a footrest, arms spread wide, flanked by the Virgin and Saint John, with a star and a crescent above the arms of the cross and Greek letters running down either side. Cut as an intaglio seal, it would have left a raised impression of the Crucifixion, a sign of its owner's faith. Its clarity and tiny scale make it an intimate Byzantine devotional object.
facts: The Met dates the seal broadly to the 9th–11th century and records it as rock crystal, about 2 cm high (accession 86.11.38, purchased 1886).
Q116273823.notes: The Greek letters were not read or verified.
